page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e3.3xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server instance configured on the KVM hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. Its compute layer provides 16 virtual CPUs derived from 8 dedicated physical cores with two threads per core. Memory capacity is substantial at 128 GB, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU distribution. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage or hardware GPU acceleration, requiring connected remote block storage for persistence.

Benchmark analysis highlights a bifurcation between single-threaded performance and parallel multi-threaded throughput. Single-core tests show constrained execution speed, with Geekbench single-core scoring 956.0 and stress-ng single-core reaching 1107.68, mirrored by lower-tier single-threaded compression rates. In contrast, multi-core benchmarks show solid middle-tier performance, producing a stress-ng multi-core score of 17371.73 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 7731.0. Uncached large-block read memory bandwidth achieves 86.27 GB/sec, supporting throughput of 21.19 million Redis SET operations per second and 11.38 GB/sec in static web serving tests.

The 1:8 compute-to-memory ratio provides effective resource density for memory-dependent applications that do not demand high single-core clocks. Typical workloads include Redis and Memcached caching tiers, medium-scale relational databases, ETL batch pipelines, and parallel enterprise application services.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e3.3xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud instance built on the KVM hypervisor and powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. It provides 16 vCPUs across 8 dedicated physical cores and 128 GB of RAM, establishing a high 1:8 vCPU-to-memory allocation. The server includes no integrated local storage and no GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks indicate modest single-thread metrics, including lower-tier compression and Geekbench single-core scores, alongside dependable mid-tier multi-threaded results such as 17,371.73 in stress-ng multi-core and 21.19 million Redis SET operations per second. Supported by instruction sets including AVX-512F and AES-NI, the instance is well suited for memory-centric enterprise workloads, in-memory caching systems like Redis, relational database backends, and multi-threaded data processing tasks that prioritize memory footprint over maximum single-core burst frequency.
